properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 4/09/2026 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Springhill Township, Fayette county. 102.4(b)8 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS – E & S plan, inspection reports and monitoring records were not available at the project site during all stages of earth disturbance activity.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 4/09/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(b)8 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS – E & S plan, inspection reports and monitoring records were not available at the project site during all stages of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8270235
Permit API: 051-23671
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Springhill Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/09/2026
Comments: On 4/09/2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of Diversified's Clemmer 6 plugged well site located in Springhill Township, Westmoreland County.According to Department records, this well was plugged on 4/16/2025. Therefore the well site restoration was due by 1/16/2026. A Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) was due by 3/17/2026. A Well Site Extension Request submitted by the operator on 12/19/2025 was returned by the Department (IR 4125309). No WSRR has been received to-date from the operator for this site. A COA was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216.The following was observed during the inspection:The former site access road is entirely unvegetated and appears to be used to access an active construction zone for a residential home. The plugged well site has not yet achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage. No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation was observed on site during this inspection. However, no temporary Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls were observed on site during this inspection. The mailbox containing the site E and S/Restoration plans was not found during this inspection. A metal pole appears to be marking the approximate coordinate location of the plugged well. No surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the approximate location of the plugged well.Based on observations from this inspection, the well site and access road are not restored. The Department recommended in IR 4125309 that the Operator fully restore the well site and access road or submit a signed and completed Post-Plugging Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration. However, no Post-Plugging WSRR or Post-Plugging Landowner Waiver has been received from the operator. Therefore, a violation shall be issued in IR 4176643 for failure to restore the well site 9 months post-plugging, in accordance with the 3/07/2019 CO and A. Violations shall be issued in this inspection for failure to have the site E and S/Restoration plan available and for failure to install temporary Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls on site.

Comments: On August 31, 2026, the Department conducted an inspection of the Oxford Dev 1 Well.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the well site was located in a wooded area. The access road appeared to be stabilized at the time of the inspection. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.At the time of inspection, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present and appeared to have all information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). There were no observed leaks or discharges of fluid at the surface around the wellhead.The production tank was located approximately 60 feet southeast of the well head. Upon inspection of the production tank, the Department observed what appeared to be a release occurring from the production tank onto the ground. A thick orange fluid was observed leaking from near the top of the tank, traveling down the side of the tank, and onto the ground. Orange and dark oil-like staining were observed on the ground in an approximate 2 foot area around the north side of the tank. Conductivity readings were taking in the thick orange fluid on the ground as well as in the dark oil like staining on the ground with readings of 0.39mS, 5.62mS, 5.81mS, and 9.72mS being obtained. These readings appeared elevated in comparison to the background conductivity reading obtained of 0.32mS.Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke to D and B Gas operator representative Brian Bittinger and informed him of the apparent release from the production tank onto the ground. Mr. Bittinger stated that he had sold the well site and has not been out there since approximately November 2025. However, he acknowledged that if the transfer has not yet been approved by the Department he is responsible and stated he would have crews onsite with in a day to remediate the spill.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Comments: On 8/31/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Orr 14 OG well in Washington Township, Fayette County. This inspection follows-up to IR 4266621, where violations were issued for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures prior to conducting earth disturbances on the access road, which is resulting in a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth. Diversified representative Jared Walker was present on site during this inspection.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- The access road appears to be a multi-use road that is shared with additional Diversified well sites. Some tire rutting was observed in the shared access road. No Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the access road entrance. Step 1.3 of the E and S/Restoration plan construction sequence is to install a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) at the access road entrance prior to conducting earth disturbances.- The well site is located within a forested agricultural area. Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed downslope of the well site. Portions of the compost filter sock are holding minor amounts of sediment. In other portions of the CFS, the stakes appear to be dislodged. This does not appear to be affecting the functionality of the CFS at the time of inspection. However, the Department recommends that the Operator conduct maintenance on the CFS. Violations may be forthcoming pending re-evaluation of this location in a future inspection. Rig mats are being installed on the saturated ground around the gas well. The E and S/Restoration plan and a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) are located at the Navaho Hollow Road entrance, which will not be used for well plugging operations. The E and S/Restoration plan is not specific to the Connellsville Street access road, which is being used for plugging operations. - The gas well is equipped with a well tag. A plugging rig and well plugging equipment have been staged on site. The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was installed on site during this inspection by Mr. Walker (Photo 24).- Upon exiting the site toward Connellsville Street, the Department observed loose soil remaining adjacent to an apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run (Photo 2). Although no sediment was observed entering this apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run at the time of inspection, it is actively under threat by this site since no E and S control measures are installed in this location. Mr. Walker stated during this inspection that an E and S/Restoration plan specific to the Connellsville Street access road is drafted, but needs to be printed and installed on site. Mr. Walker also stated that correction of the ongoing threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOTC), and installation of a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) and additional CFS will be conducted on the day following this inspection.The Department continues to recommend that the operator take immediate action to cease ongoing threats to the Waters of the Commonwealth.Based on today's inspection, the violations for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures will remain outstanding, as the threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth remains and tire rutting is occurring on site. Additional violations are being issued for failure to follow the E and S/Restoration plan and for failure to have an updated copy of the E and S/Restoration plan available on site.The violation issued in IR 4265922 for failure to post the Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) on site will be closed in IR 4269231.

Comments: Inspection conducted in response to a spill notification received yesterday 2/26/19 about a release of an estimated 10 gallons of produced water that had occurred at 1730 the same day. Mike Deming of SWN met me on location upon my arrival. He explained that an 18-wheeler off-loading produced water from a battery of frac tanks had inadvertently pumped produced water out of the truck into the tank instead of pumping it out of the tank and into the truck. This activated a pressure relief valve on the truck which led to the release of the produced water. Mr. Deming said that a vacuum truck on site immediately sucked up the fluid and gravel from the pad surface was scraped with a skid steer and placed into a container for disposal. At the time of this inspection, the site was snow-covered and the impacted gravel material had already been removed. During the inspection, a zipper frac was in process on the 10H and 5H wells. The site was in good shape overall. The secondary containment appeared to be fully intact with no visible damage. Fresh water was being pumped in from a FWI as well as trucked in to the site. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Comments: On 12/06/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well site production tanks following violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) being noted and immediately corrected on 11/08/2023 due to prompt remediation measures. I was accompanied by Paul Stiner of Diversified, Albatros representative, and remediation personal. Adjacent to the tanks, the F23 well was being swabbed. The following was observed during inspection:The area within the earthern berm that contained water with elevated readings was being excavated and gravel to be added. A sump was dug and fluids vacced out. Tanks 1 and 2 to be removed.Some elevated conductivity readings within the water were noted within the sump behind tank 3 and nearby (Photos 1-6).A sheen was seen within the water behind tank 4; this sheen appeared to be a combination of biological material and production fluid. Reading taken behind tank yielded high results (Photos 7-10).Relatively high readings in water and sediment in front of tanks 1 and 2 (Photos 11-17). Readings under tank 5 valve and behind tank 5 were relatively high (Photos 18, 19).Material excavated was in a lined dumpster. I recommend to ensure liner does not continue to fall (Photo 20).A dozer was onsite to correct the access road leading to additional wells on the property (Photo 22). Rig onsite for swabbing of F23 (Photo 23).Manure around site yields high readings, however this is common. A comparible reading was taken at a low spot at the base of the earthern berm and it displayed an acceptable reading of 1.80 mS. This well in in a horse pasture (Photos 24, 25).Due to current remediation measures, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being noted and immediately corrected. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending further inspection.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-02-27
Comments: On February 27, 2019 Department representative Sue Herzing conducted a incident related inspection at EQT Production's Turkey Well Pad. I met with EQT Senior Compressor Technician Dan Canton on the access road on my way into the Turkey Well Pad. The spill occurred between producing wells 033-27049 and 033-27051. A 130 gallon corrosion inhibitor tote was stationed and connected between both wells. EQT claims that during the recent high winds storm that occurred on Sunday 2/24/19 through Monday 2/25/19, that winds over turned this 130 gallon tote; resulting in ~30 gallons of corrosion inhibitor being released on the well pad. When I arrived onsite the spill had already been cleaned up and contaminated soils were placed in a lined roll-off box still stationed onsite. The impacted area is triangular in shape ~6 ft. wide and ~8 ft. long (see photos 2-4). New rock was placed in the impacted area. A soil probe was used to screen the rock covered impacted area. No elevated conductivity in the soil/rock were detected. Violations have been noted and immediately corrected.

Comments: On September 21, 2023, inspection conducted at the Rumpelstiltskin well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3582382 where violations were issued in response to a spill caused by a GPU dumpline failure.The following was observed:At the time of inspection, the Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The ERP was onsite (see photos 2 and 3). Some erosion rills were observed in the access road (see photos 4 and 5). Secondary containment was added to the GPU units onsite, and the impacted area was backfilled (see photos 10 and 11). A well tag was present on well 6H, with no observed leaks or discharge on the ground around it, and it appeared to be equipped for production (see photo 13). There are three other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 8). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 12). Seven rolloff dumpsters labeled "production water impacted solids" were onsite (see photos 7 and 9). After inspection was conducted, the Department spoke via phone with EQT representative David Crayne, who stated that remediation was complete and Act 2 is nearly ready for submittal to ECB. Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that maintenance be conducted on the access road to prevent worsening accelerated erosion and sedimentation onsite. Closure of violations shall be contingent upon Act 2 approval and a subsequent CEI inspection.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/01/2024
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8203235
Permit API: 125-26999
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Hopewell Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/01/2024
Comments: On October 1, 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection at the R Carlisle well pad in Hopewell Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination was approved for this site on October 28, 2016.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Several portions of the access road are exhibiting severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation at the time of inspection (see photo 2). The well pad appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed (see photo 3). Production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 4). The GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 5). However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of fluid leaks or discharge was observed on the ground around the GPU units. Well 7H is equipped with a well tag with no observable fluids leaking to the ground around it (see photos 7 and 8). There are four other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 6). Containment is staged adjacent to the production tanks, which appears to be for pumping operations. It is approximately half-full of rainwater at the time of inspection (see photo 9). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 10). Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that secondary containments are kept empty so they are able to mitigate the risk of a release from occurring on site as intended. The Department also recommends that GPU units and other primary containments that store regulated substances are equipped with secondary containments to mitigate the risk of discharge to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth.Violations are being issued against the severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation observed in the access road.

CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/04/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8223441
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/04/2025
Comments: On 03/04/2025 representatives from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 34F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).All standing water observed on the pad surface was frozen solid.There are 2 recently completed wells onsite and their American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers are posted at the site entrance; I was unable to confirm if the wells were tagged due to them currently being covered (photos #1 and 2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are held in a secondary containment structure which did not contain any standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the containment structure did not contain any standing water. The tanks were labeled as per the Department's request (photos #5 and 6). A dehydration unit is also noted onsite and held in secondary containment (photo #7).Numerous upright brine tanks and temporary storage tanks are still noted onsite and held in their respective secondary containment structures which appear to be functioning as intended (photos #8 and 9). Multiple lined and covered residual waste containers are in use onsite for ongoing Act 2 remediation efforts as well as disassembly of the pad wide containment system (rig matting) and tear down of completions equipment (photos #10 and 11). The modular aboveground storage structures (MASS) have been removed and the brine offload area has been disassembled (photo #12).Remediation remains ongoing from the releases on 12/04/2024 and 12/09/2024 (Inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285) as the areas formerly covered by rig matting and containment structures are now accessible. Pad drainage systems remain shut in to prevent any water from ice and snow melt from leaving the pad. I did not observe any diesel sheen on the pad surface. Water is being removed from the well pad via an onsite vacuum truck as it accumulates. The area located underneath the brine offload area from the release on 12/09/2024 is currently being excavated to comply with Act 2 remediation standards (photo #13). Soil in this area field measured for electrical conductivity at ~1.68mS/cm and fluids accumulating in this area field measured for EC at ~15.67mS/cm (photos #14 and 15). These soils and fluids are being collected via vacuum truck or lined residual waste container.Site stabilization could not be adequately assessed at the time of this inspection due to snow coverage. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review in the mailbox at the site entrance (photo #16). No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #17). The basin inlet remains shut in and no fluids or diesel sheen was observed (photo #18). Soil in the basin field measured for EC at ~0.72mS/cm (photo #19).Violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Unconventional: No

Comments: On 8/31/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Orr 14 OG well in Washington Township, Fayette County. This inspection follows-up to IR 4266621, where violations were issued for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures prior to conducting earth disturbances on the access road, which is resulting in a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth. Diversified representative Jared Walker was present on site during this inspection.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- The access road appears to be a multi-use road that is shared with additional Diversified well sites. Some tire rutting was observed in the shared access road. No Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the access road entrance. Step 1.3 of the E and S/Restoration plan construction sequence is to install a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) at the access road entrance prior to conducting earth disturbances.- The well site is located within a forested agricultural area. Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed downslope of the well site. Portions of the compost filter sock are holding minor amounts of sediment. In other portions of the CFS, the stakes appear to be dislodged. This does not appear to be affecting the functionality of the CFS at the time of inspection. However, the Department recommends that the Operator conduct maintenance on the CFS. Violations may be forthcoming pending re-evaluation of this location in a future inspection. Rig mats are being installed on the saturated ground around the gas well. The E and S/Restoration plan and a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) are located at the Navaho Hollow Road entrance, which will not be used for well plugging operations. The E and S/Restoration plan is not specific to the Connellsville Street access road, which is being used for plugging operations. - The gas well is equipped with a well tag. A plugging rig and well plugging equipment have been staged on site. The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was installed on site during this inspection by Mr. Walker (Photo 24).- Upon exiting the site toward Connellsville Street, the Department observed loose soil remaining adjacent to an apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run (Photo 2). Although no sediment was observed entering this apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run at the time of inspection, it is actively under threat by this site since no E and S control measures are installed in this location. Mr. Walker stated during this inspection that an E and S/Restoration plan specific to the Connellsville Street access road is drafted, but needs to be printed and installed on site. Mr. Walker also stated that correction of the ongoing threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOTC), and installation of a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) and additional CFS will be conducted on the day following this inspection.The Department continues to recommend that the operator take immediate action to cease ongoing threats to the Waters of the Commonwealth.Based on today's inspection, the violations for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures will remain outstanding, as the threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth remains and tire rutting is occurring on site. Additional violations are being issued for failure to follow the E and S/Restoration plan and for failure to have an updated copy of the E and S/Restoration plan available on site.The violation issued in IR 4265922 for failure to post the Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) on site will be closed in IR 4269231.
